recipes.goal: Shape failed numeric route/query binding in an endpoint filter before handler execution; retain ThrowOnBadRequest=false in Development and distinguish earlier body-read failures.

selectionNotes: Scalar binding failures with a registered filter; Development requires ThrowOnBadRequest=false. Handler execution is not required.
This behavior is also verified on .NET 10; .NET 11 release-note placement does not make it a new exclusive API. Malformed JSON can return before filters.

prerequisites: Create every file below in a standalone ParcelIntake directory for the chosen target. Empty Directory files isolate surrounding build/package rules. Restore the matching framework packs once; installed guidance itself remains offline. SDK 10.0.402 / 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 and C# 14.0 / 15.0 reproduce actual evidence, not minimum language-feature requirements.
constraints: Set RouteHandlerOptions.ThrowOnBadRequest=false explicitly in Development. Otherwise BadHttpRequestException leaves binding before a filter can shape the failure. This setting is the normal non-Development default; it does not suppress arbitrary handler exceptions.

Inspect HttpContext.Response.StatusCode==400 at filter entry, before next(context). Failed arguments may contain defaults or nulls: do not dereference or repair them, call business services or call next on that path. A 400 produced later by the handler is a separate domain decision and must retain its own body.

Scope the filter to the endpoints whose binding-error contract you own. A status code is not a typed diagnostic: an earlier component could also set 400. Do not install another earlier status writer and assume every 400 means numeric binding failed.

In the tested .NET 10/11 RequestDelegateFactory path, malformed JSON and unsupported content types return before the filter: empty 400 and 415 respectively in this app. No ProblemDetails service or status pages are configured in the control. Use a separately configured ProblemDetails/status-code middleware policy for broader body-read failures; this filter is not universal exception or JSON error handling.

The original .NET 10 comparison uses the same valid filter technique and passes the same actual requests. No older workaround is required. The .NET 10 source already contains scalar-failure filter invocation. The .NET 10 directory is comparison evidence, not an additional curated foundation or advertised target-10 route.

Numeric route values must reach binding: a route constraint such as {dock:int} can reject the route earlier with 404. These samples deliberately use {dock}. Binding failures are different from model/business validation; no automatic validation service is enabled.

recipes.goal: Run a public standalone endpoint immediately after routing with ShortCircuitAttribute, while keeping endpoints that need authentication, CORS or other downstream middleware on the ordinary pipeline.

selectionNotes: Standalone responses only: must not require skipped authentication, CORS or other middleware. Middleware before UseRouting still runs.
The .NET 10 ShortCircuit() convention remains valid on .NET 11; the attribute is the newer declarative form.

SDK 10.0.402 / 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 and C# 14.0 / 15.0 reproduce actual evidence, not minimum language-feature requirements.
constraints: Use only for a deliberately public, self-contained response that does not need skipped authentication, CORS, antiforgery, rate limiting, session, telemetry enrichment or any other downstream middleware. Audit default/fallback policies and custom checks too: the framework cannot discover every application-specific dependency.

Short-circuiting runs the endpoint during UseRouting and omits the remaining middleware. Middleware placed before UseRouting still executes. Place any checks that must apply to every request before routing or keep the endpoint on the ordinary pipeline. The endpoint still executes; short-circuiting does not mean returning without its handler.

With the default security-metadata checks, combining short-circuit metadata with authorization or CORS metadata throws InvalidOperationException. Required antiforgery metadata on relevant form methods is also rejected. Do not suppress those checks to make an unsafe endpoint work; remove short-circuiting from endpoints that need those protections.

The optional status code supplies the response status before the endpoint executes; it does not remove the endpoint, authorize callers or guarantee the final result will not set another status. The retained convention sample returns plain text with status 202.

The new attribute is in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing and implements IShortCircuitMetadata. It targets methods/classes, is not inherited and is single-use per target. It can be placed on a controller/action or Minimal API handler; this canonical proof selects Minimal APIs. The existing ShortCircuit() convention remains valid; the .NET 10 sample uses it for the same goal.

The X-Test-Crew authentication scheme and developer exception page exist only to expose the local comparison. Never trust that client header as a production credential or expose developer exception details in production. No performance saving, browser CORS enforcement, proxy behavior or production security configuration is measured here.
